profile.headline: Full Stack Developer | Building Productivity Tools
profile.summary:
Full stack engineer with ~10 years of experience, spanning frontend platform work in React at LiveRamp and backend + infrastructure work on a payments platform at Teambridge. I tend to gravitate toward whatever piece of a project is the current bottleneck, which has kept me usefully unspecialized.
I do my best work on teams that don't draw hard lines between roles, and I'm partial to durable abstractions, clear interfaces, and tools that make other engineers faster.

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.locationName: San Francisco, California, United States · Hybrid
positions.description:
Working across the stack on Teambridge's Pay platform — payroll calculation and Instant Pay, our Earned Wage Access product. Primarily Kotlin/Micronaut on the backend, Postgres, React/TypeScript on the admin surfaces, AWS infrastructure managed via Terraform.

A few of the larger things I've led:
• Trust Evaluation rule engine — designed and built the system that determines worker eligibility for Instant Pay. Schema-driven, so we can onboard customers with non-standard pay structures through configuration rather than code changes.
• Automated Instant Pay invoicing and ACH reconciliation end-to-end — invoice generation, delivery, payin matching, exception handling. Removed the manual eng + CS work of creating invoices, coordinating delivery, and matching repayment wires by hand, which let us scale Instant Pay volume without a proportional increase in ops cost.
• Carried-balance migration of the payroll calculation engine, which unlocked accurate multi-period reconciliation. Added Redis distributed locks around Instant Pay payouts to close a double-pay race under concurrency.
• Pay platform on-call infrastructure from a sparse baseline — Datadog ingestion, monitors and escalation policies, and a GitHub Actions release-cut workflow that replaced a manual checklist.
• Broader backend reliability work — reporting endpoint performance, structured logging across async paths, and a tolerant permissions deserializer that let us ship a schema migration without taking down login.

Tech: Kotlin, Micronaut, Postgres, Redis, Kotlin Coroutines, React, TypeScript, AWS (ECS, RDS, SNS, SQS), Terraform, Datadog, GitHub Actions.

positions.title: Full Stack Developer
positions.description:
Spent most of my time on frontend platform work — building the foundations other teams used to ship UI consistently. Certified Scrum Master for a squad of seven engineers and a product manager.

• Co-founded LiveRamp's internal React component library in partnership with our design team — became the source of truth for visual consistency across the application and seeded a broader culture of component reuse across the engineering org.
• Built a UI generation toolkit (paired Ruby gem and NPM package) that let backend engineers add configurable models without pulling in a full-stack dev, materially cutting the time to extend backend models.
• Conceptualized and built a React App Manager that made page-by-page migration to React viable inside a legacy framework — shared store, reusable reducers, DevTools wired in.
• Designed and shipped the self-service ingestion API and UI as part of a cross-team group, replacing a series of one-off integrations with a stable customer-facing path.
• Stood up monitoring and alerting across the ingestion pipelines, cutting customer-facing response times and giving on-call real visibility into pipeline health.

Tech: Ruby on Rails, React, Redux, JavaScript, SQL, GCP, Git.
